```{exercise, name = "Non-normal bivariate random variable", label = nnbivrv}
Find a non-normal bivariate random variable $(X, Y)$ with normal marginals.

Hint: there are many possible solutions. Try starting with $N(0, I)$, but set density to zero when $XY < 0$.
```

<div class="fold">
```{solution, echo = togs}
Let $\varphi(t) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \exp(-t^2/2)$ be the univariate standard normal density.
The following bivariate density is one possible solution:
\begin{align}
    p_{XY}(x,y) = 2 \varphi(x)\varphi(y) \; \textrm{if}\; xy>0\textrm{, and 0 otherwise.}
\end{align}
We multiply by $2$ because we took away half the total mass from the original bivariate normal.
```
```{proof, echo = togs}
Let $f(x) = \int_{0}^\infty p_{XY}(x, y) dy$ and $g(x) = \int_{-\infty}^0 p_{XY}(x, y) dy$.
The marginal $p_X(x)$ is then:
\begin{align}
    p_X(x) = \int_{-\infty}^\infty p_{XY}(x, y) dy = \begin{cases}
        f(x), & x \ge 0, \\
        g(x),  & x < 0.
    \end{cases}
\end{align}

\noindent
Simplify $f(x)$:
\begin{align}
    f(x) = \int_{0}^\infty p_{XY}(x, y) dy = 2\varphi(x) \int_{0}^\infty \varphi(y) dy = 2\varphi(x) \frac{1}{2} = \varphi(x)
\end{align}

\noindent
Simplify $g(x)$:
\begin{align}
    f(x) = \int_{-\infty}^0 p_{XY}(x, y) dy  2\varphi(x) \int_{-\infty}^0 \varphi(y) dy = 2\varphi(x) \frac{1}{2} = \varphi(x)
\end{align}

\noindent
Since $f(x) = g(x) = \varphi(x)$, we conclude that $p_X(x) = \varphi(x)$ regardless of $x$. Therefore $X \sim N(0, 1)$ and $Y \sim N(0, 1)$ by symmetry.
```
</div>
